label: What Irreducible Means
subgoals: A nonconstant polynomial is irreducible when it factors only through a unit and a constant multiple of itself.
Over a field the degree of a factor must be strictly smaller.

label: Counting over Finite Fields
subgoals: The number of monic irreducibles of degree n over a field with p elements follows a divisor formula.
For small n the count can be checked by listing candidates.

label: Testing a Candidate
subgoals: The polynomial x squared plus one is irreducible over the reals and reducible over the complex numbers.
Over a finite field its status depends on whether minus one is a square.
